objections.claim: The rebaseline guard is `isPlainObject(open.baseline_by_model_class)`, which `{}` satisfies. The spec never establishes that the open span's baseline is non-empty, nor that it agrees with `ledger.budget.tokens_at_start`. If a run has a non-zero mint `tokens_at_start` and an open span whose `baseline_by_model_class` is `{}` (the spec's own fixture shape), the rebaseline sets `tokensAtStart = byModelClassTotal({}) = 0`, so the transcript branch computes `max(0, measuredTotal - 0) + closedSpend.total` — the full transcript sum including prior-session history. On a resumed run with closed spans, `has_closed_spans AND rebaseline_applied` are both true, so the inflation warning is *suppressed* — a silently inflated total, the precise defect the ticket's premise says it eliminates.
objections.evidence: §3 step 2 ("IF budgetSessions AND currentOpenSpan(budgetSessions)?.baseline_by_model_class is a plain object: tokensAtStart = byModelClassTotal(open.baseline_by_model_class)"); §5 fixture shows `baseline_by_model_class: {}` for both spans; §4 edge case "Open span with a null/missing baseline" only guards null/missing, not empty; the §5 rebaseline scenario uses a *non-empty* baseline `{m1:{input:50}}`, so the spec never tests the empty-baseline-with-nonzero-tokens_at_start case it itself fixtures.
objections.predicted_consequence: A real resumed run whose open span carries an empty baseline (as the fixture models) reports `tokens_total = measuredTotal + closedSpend.total` instead of `measuredTotal - tokens_at_start + closedSpend.total`, with the inflation warning suppressed — the two governance surfaces disagree again, in the inflated direction, and the regression test suite (which uses `tokens_at_start: 0`) will not catch it.

objections.claim: §2 argues the follow-up enumerator must live in a shared read-side module, "not buried in the budget-*governor* module, so a future consumer does not reach into governance bookkeeping for a reading primitive." Yet this very fix has economics import `closedSessionsSpend`/`currentOpenSpan`/`byModelClassTotal` from `budget.js` — reaching into governance bookkeeping for reading primitives. The same reasoning that keeps the enumerator out of the governor would argue for extracting these accumulation helpers to the shared read-side module. As shipped, economics' correctness permanently tracks budget.js's internal span semantics; a future budget.js change (e.g., FAFF-594 window logic, a new span shape) silently changes economics.
objections.evidence: §2 "Placement (follow-up decision)… not buried in the budget-*governor* module"; §3 "The reused pure helpers (imported from `budget.js`)".
objections.predicted_consequence: The first follow-up slice (the `runOwnedTranscriptFiles` enumerator) lands in a new read-side module while the accumulation helpers stay in the governor, leaving two read-side consumers with split homes and a permanent economics→governor dependency that the spec's own placement principle argues against.

objections.claim: The guard assumes a resume always produces a closed span (`owner.epoch > 1` AND `NOT hasClosedSpans` → warn). The spec never establishes that the resume writer always closes the prior epoch's span; a prior epoch with no measurable spend could legitimately be left as an open span (the spec's own "all spans open" edge case treats open spans as a valid shape). On such a resumed run, `owner.epoch > 1` with no closed span fires the shape-drift warning on a legitimate state, not a drift.
objections.evidence: §3 "shape_drift: owner.epoch > 1 (a resume happened) BUT no closed span was detected"; §4 edge case "budget.sessions present, all spans open… Correct: … no warning" (scoped to fresh runs only, without establishing why a resumed run cannot also be all-open).
objections.predicted_consequence: A resumed run whose prior epoch recorded no measurable spend emits a spurious "ledger shape may predate budget.sessions[]" warning, training readers to ignore the shape-drift signal — the same warning-fatigue the spec's inflation-warning refinement is explicitly trying to avoid.

objections.claim: The entire warning system (coverage, estimate, provenance, shape-drift) gates on `hasClosedSpans`, and the shape-drift guard that is supposed to close the fail-open only fires when `Number(ledger.owner?.epoch) > 1`. A resumed run whose ledger predates the epoch counter (or whose resume did not bump it) has `owner.epoch` absent → `Number(undefined)` is `NaN` → `NaN > 1` is false → no drift warning, no coverage warning, and the earlier epoch is dropped with zero signal. That is precisely the "silent epoch-scoped figure" the ticket's own principle forbids, and the guard fails open on exactly the legacy-shape case the spec itself acknowledges ("the ledger shape may predate budget.sessions[]").
objections.evidence: §3 `shape_drift: bool # owner.epoch > 1 (a resume happened) BUT no closed span was detected`; §4 edge case "Resume happened but no closed span found (`owner.epoch > 1`, `hasClosedSpans == false`) — shape drift"; §3 "Never silently drop; if you cannot span, say so — on EVERY path"; assumption "a resumed run's ledger carries `budget.sessions[]`" is validated only against current `resume.js`, not against legacy shapes.
objections.predicted_consequence: A resumed run on a pre-epoch-counter ledger (or a resume path that fails to bump `owner.epoch`) reports an epoch-scoped `tokens_total` with no warning, indistinguishable from a fresh single-epoch run — the exact silent-drop defect the ticket exists to close, surviving the fix. Checkable: run the synthetic fixture with `owner.epoch` removed/undefined and assert the shape-drift warning fires; it will not.

objections.claim: The scenario asserts economics "meters epoch-0" under `--session-id epoch-0`, but the only observable it pins is that `tokens_total` is *different* from the open-span case. The fixture names only `epoch-1.jsonl` as a transcript; no epoch-0 transcript is specified, so the expected `tokens_total` for `--session-id epoch-0` is never pinned. A build that honors the flag but meters the *ambient* session (the unrelated prior-session id the scenario itself says is wrong) also produces a different `tokens_total` and passes.
objections.evidence: §5 scenario "Given a resumed 2-epoch ledger / When `faff economics --run-dir <fixture> --session-id <epoch-0> --json` is run / Then the --session-id flag overrides the open-span session and economics meters epoch-0 … a build that ignores the flag and meters the open span produces a different tokens_total and fails". The assertion is only inequality; the DONE item "`--session-id <flag>` overrides the open-span session (FAFF-488 contract preserved)" inherits the same weak oracle.
objections.predicted_consequence: The FAFF-488 precedence AC is decided by "any value ≠ 600", so a build that selects the wrong session (ambient, or any third id) while honoring the flag ships green. The test cannot tell "meters epoch-0" from "meters something else".

objections.claim: Every warning-asserting scenario (the four `--by day|mcp|effort|phase` coverage warnings, the estimate-path warning, the inflation-warning suppression, the inflation-warning still-fires null-baseline case, the shape-drift warning, the zero-delta presence-gated warning, and the degraded-provenance bullet) asserts a warning exists or is absent, but the spec never names where warnings appear — a JSON field, stderr, or something else. §3 shows a `warnings:` list being pushed to but never says where it lands in the output. The scenarios all run `--json`, so the test must know whether to read a JSON field or capture stderr.
objections.evidence: §3 `computeUnitEconomics` warning block (seven `push` statements, no output field named); §5 scenarios asserting "emits the coverage warning", "a warning names the estimate", "the inflation warning STILL fires", "the shape-drift warning fires", "the coverage warning still fires" — none names the observation point.
objections.predicted_consequence: A build that emits warnings to a different channel than the test author assumed (or that the existing `tokens_at_start=0` warning uses) fails the warning assertions for reasons unrelated to the spec's behaviour, or passes while hiding warnings where a reader cannot see them. The oracle for ~7 scenarios is "wherever warnings happen to be", which the spec never pins.

objections.claim: The rebaseline scenario asserts "rebaseline_applied == true", but §3 lists `rebaseline_applied` as an *input* to `computeUnitEconomics`, never as an output field. The observable consequence (the rebaselined `tokensTotal` via `transcriptPortion`) does carry the AC, but the scenario's direct assertion of the flag has no observation point.
objections.evidence: §5 rebaseline scenario "Then tokensAtStart is rebaselined to 50 … and rebaseline_applied == true"; §3 INPUT list includes `rebaseline_applied: bool` with no output counterpart.
objections.predicted_consequence: The test can only decide the AC via `tokensTotal`; the "rebaseline_applied == true" half of the scenario is unassertable as written, so a build that rebaselines the numbers but never sets the flag (or sets it wrongly) is indistinguishable from a correct one on this scenario.

objections.claim: §3 specifies the warning as `"tokens_at_start=0 — run total may be inflated by prior-session history"`, while the suppression scenario quotes it as `"tokens_at_start=0 — may be inflated by prior-session history"`. If a test asserts presence or absence by matching the quoted string, the two texts disagree.
objections.evidence: §3 warning block vs §5 "the 'tokens_at_start=0 — may be inflated by prior-session history' warning is ABSENT".
objections.predicted_consequence: A test written against one quoted text fails against a build that emits the other; the spec gives no single canonical string to assert.

objections.claim: The estimate-path scenario says "the RESUMING epoch's transcript missing (tokens_source falls back to 'estimate')" but never specifies how the fixture makes the transcript missing — absent file, empty file, or some other signal. The build agent must infer the trigger from existing `economics.js` code, and the scenario's numeric (200) depends on that inference being right.
objections.evidence: §5 estimate-path scenario "the RESUMING epoch's transcript missing (tokens_source falls back to 'estimate', e.g. attempts × est_per == 200)"; no fixture mechanism named.
objections.predicted_consequence: If the actual fallback trigger differs from what the test author assumes (e.g. the code requires a flag, or an empty file does not trigger it), the fixture never reaches the estimate branch and the scenario's 200 assertion is vacuous or fails spuriously.

objections.claim: The parity DONE item and scenario assert byte-for-byte identity with pre-change output, but the spec never says how that reference is obtained — a golden fixture, a captured run of the current code, or reuse of existing single-session assertions in `test/economics.test.mjs`. The parenthetical in the scenario ("closedSpend.total == 0, hasClosedSpans == false, rebaseline_applied == false") names internal flags, not observable output.
objections.evidence: §8 DONE "produces byte-for-byte-identical economics output to pre-change"; §5 parity scenario "the output is byte-for-byte identical to the pre-change output".
objections.predicted_consequence: The test author must invent the reference mechanism; two authors could pick different references and disagree on whether the AC passed. The parity gate is not decided by the spec as written.

objections.claim: The DONE item "A folded span with `close_source != "transcript"` surfaces a provenance warning, threaded via `degraded_close_sources`" is backed only by a trailing bullet in §5 ("On a resumed 2-epoch ledger whose closed span … carries `close_source: "degraded"` … a warning names epoch-0's measurement basis as degraded"), not a formal Given/When/Then with a pass/fail assertion. The bullet also inherits the unspecified warnings channel.
objections.evidence: §8 DONE provenance item; §5 trailing bullet after the holdout list.
objections.predicted_consequence: The provenance AC has no born-verifiable scenario; a build that drops the provenance warning entirely would pass every formal scenario and only fail an informal bullet.
